alternative_explanations: Any gain may come entirely from an explicit one-dimensional convergence coordinate already represented inside the learned transition rather than from transferable adaptive computation.
Dense transition accounting may make halting look favorable only because zero or low-rank weights are executed as a full matrix.
confounds: One visible synthetic low-rank attractor, one seed, train depths at most four, OOD depth six, exact event tokenization and deterministic convergence limit external validity.
The oracle receives true required depth and is a capability-cost bound only.
falsification_criteria: The learned halt policy has below 0.95 accuracy on any registered depth, stops prematurely on D=6 OOD, or its transition calls fail to track required depth.
A residual, transition-gate or fixed control matches capability while dominating the learned policy in full workload, state and fit accounting.

outcome_policy.negative: Discard the tested controller without tuning if it halts prematurely, fails OOD length transfer, or loses the quality-work trade-off to fixed max.
outcome_policy.null: Preserve adaptive stopping as a classical implementation pattern but return HYP-0004 to dormant if the shared gate or residual achieves the same savings more cheaply.
outcome_policy.positive: Keep HYP-0004 testing and preregister a multi-seed adversarial screen only if learned halting is exact on D=6 and non-dominated by both transition-gate and residual controls.

predicted_outcome: Adaptive policies should make transition calls track true convergence depth and reduce balanced full workload versus fixed-max because every dense learned transition is expensive; the decisive uncertainty is whether a learned controller remains non-dominated after comparing with the shared transition's own gate and a residual stop.
promotion_criteria: Quick cannot promote; only exact OOD capability and non-dominated full workload against transition-gate and residual controls may justify a three-seed adversarial screen.
research_question: When fixed and adaptive solvers share exactly the same learned nonlinear recurrent transition and raw input, can a learned halt policy preserve train and longer-depth OOD capability while reducing full-system work beyond fixed-depth, residual and transition-gate controls?
title: Adaptive compute with an identical learned nonlinear transition
